text: Rules are evaluated by Drools embedded in each of the 19 services, in the service that owns the decision, and the package registry, versions and governance sit in rwb-decision (P7).
why: Version 3 embeds Drools in the single recovery module; Architecture v5 slide 27 and the Temporal and Drools design slide 11 put the evaluation in the owning service and the registry in rwb-decision (ADR-017, DP-04).
read: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 11, 24, 27, 41; Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slides 11 to 13; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-04; ids.json ADR-017
confirm: Architecture review confirms ADR-017 before Wave 1.
impact: Every service carries the KIE libraries, its own evaluator and its own model cache; the registry is one service, not 19.

text: S2 rwb-treatment owns and evaluates the PAYMENT_MATCH package; the matchPayments activity of P8 rwb-payment asks S2 for the answer through S2's contract.
why: The Temporal and Drools design slide 18 gives S2 the three Phase 1 packages; Architecture v5 slide 14 puts the matchPayments activity in rwb-payment, which then needs a caller path to the model's owner rather than a second copy of it.
read: Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 18; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 14 and 41; Ownership Map v1 Workflows and activities
confirm: RW-COE and the P8 and S2 owners agree the package owner when E2-042 is authored.
impact: If P8 is confirmed as the evaluator, one column of the section 2 table changes and the model load path of P8 is added.

text: RuleCatalog, RulePackageRepository, rule_package, rule_package_version, rule_row and rule_test_case are served by rwb-decision (P7); an owning service asks the registry through its published contract and keeps no copy of the catalogue.
why: The Ownership Map places the four tables with P7 in schema rwb_decision, while version 3 publishes RuleCatalog as an interface of the one runtime.
read: Ownership Map v1 Tables sheet (rule_package, rule_package_version, rule_row, rule_test_case) and Rulings sheet; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 14, 27 and 41; ids.json (rule package registry ruling in Template and Rules R3)
confirm: P7 confirms the catalog read contract in API Specification v5.
impact: A catalogue read is one REST hop to rwb-decision; no service schema carries rule_row.

text: The Import line of a workbook names the fact class of the owning service, in the Java package th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.<short without hyphen> of Rules R4; the exact class names of the 448 rules are not specified in the sources and are left as the placeholder.
why: Version 3 names recovery.casewf.rules.facts.AllocationFacts, a class of the single module, which does not exist once the service is split; Rules R4 fixes the per-service Java package but not the class names.
read: Rules Engine Design v3 section 3; Template and Rules R4
confirm: RW-COE confirms the class names when each package is authored.
impact: The workbook format is unchanged; only the Import cell differs per service.

text: An owning service fetches an approved model with GET /rule-models/{n}/{v} on rwb-decision under /api/recovery/decision/v1; the exact operation name, path and payload are confirmed in API Specification v5 and are the placeholder until then.
why: Architecture v5 slides 14 and 27 name the fetch, and the Ownership Map Endpoints sheet does not carry it, so neither a published operation nor a payload exists in the sources read.
read: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 14, 18 and 27; Ownership Map v1 Endpoints sheet; Rules R4 REST base
confirm: P7 publishes the operation in API Specification v5 and the Ownership Map gains the row.
impact: If the operation is not published in Wave 1 the model swap falls back to the version in the deployment, which would break the no-release rule change.

text: The delivery table keeps the story set and releases of version 3 and adds the capability owner only: the registry and every /admin/rule-package endpoint are P7 rwb-decision, and the embedded kit is PLT with the per-service delta under DP-04.
why: The split plan gives RWB-E1-072 the primary PLT and RWB-E1-073 the primary P3 with a P7 slice, while the Ownership Map gives every rule endpoint to P7; the document states the owner without changing the story set.
read: _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json legacy entries for RWB-E1-072, RWB-E1-073, RWB-E2-041 and RWB-E2-042; Ownership Map v1 Endpoints sheet; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-04
confirm: The backlog owner confirms the story split when the story files are issued.
impact: No story is re-scoped by this document; only the owner of each deliverable is named.

text: The decision record, the state change and the outbox row are written by one RecordAndApply activity in one transaction in the owning service's schema, and DecisionRecorded is published to rwb.decision-record.v1 for the central ledger in rwb-decision.
why: ADR-022 writes the record and the change together, so the two activities of version 3 (WriteDecisionLogActivity and ApplyStateActivity) become one; the Temporal and Drools design states the same merge.
read: Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 14; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 20, 22 and 28; ids.json ADR-022
confirm: Risk and Internal Audit sign off the ledger model (Architecture v5 slide 39 decision 5).
impact: One activity and one transaction replace two activities; the steps of section 7 lose one entry and gain one.

text: The effective-date step keeps the name RulePackageEffectiveDateJob and runs as JOB-20, a Temporal Schedule at 00:01 in rwb-decision (P7), which publishes RulePackageInForce (EV-30); the Quartz job is retired under ADR-016.
why: Architecture v5 slide 44 gives JOB-20 to rwb-decision as a Schedule and retires the shared Quartz tables, while version 3 names a Quartz job owned by RW-COE.
read: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 31 and 44; Ownership Map v1 Jobs sheet JOB-20; ids.json ADR-016
confirm: The platform team confirms the Schedule in Wave 0.
impact: One Schedule replaces one Quartz job; no shared scheduler table is used.

text: The 93-table count of Physical Schema v6 is kept as the count of the target table set; the four rule tables are in schema rwb_decision with login rwb_decision, and the distribution of the 93 over the 19 schemas is the split work of RWB-PLT-NF06-DB.
why: Version 3 counts one schema; Architecture v5 and ADR-014 give every service its own schema and login, so the count is no longer a schema count.
read: Rules Engine Design v3 section 8; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 29 and 41; Template and Rules R6 (RWB-PLT-NF06-DB); Ownership Map v1 Tables sheet
confirm: ACE DBA confirms the schema split at Wave 0.
impact: The physical schema folder carries 19 rwb_<name>.sql files; the registry tables are created by the rwb_decision script.

text: The UNIVERSAL package is evaluated in every service from its own loaded copy of the same approved version, with authoring, scenarios, four-eyes approval and effective dating in rwb-decision (P7).
why: Version 3 gives every package one owning service, and the temporal design states that the universal rules apply in every service; the two hold only if the package is loaded everywhere and governed once.
read: Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 13; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 27 and 41
confirm: RW-COE confirms the UNIVERSAL load in Epic 3.
impact: Every service consumes RulePackageInForce for UNIVERSAL as well as for its own route set.

text: Every owner named in this document is the code and service of the Microservice Ownership Map v1 and _work/msr/plan/ownership.json, never a name taken from a story master, and no name of a person appears anywhere.
why: Template and Rules R3 and R4 fix the owners and the naming; the run rules forbid names of people.
read: Ownership Map v1 Services, Tables, Endpoints, Events, Workflows and activities, Jobs and Rulings sheets; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json; AGENTS.md rule 4
impact: Owners are stable codes; a role change does not change the document.

text: Version 4 is issued as Draft: no approval of this version is recorded in this run, and the version 3 approval path (RW-RISK on each package) is unchanged.
why: The run records no human approval and never asks for one; a missing approval or status is an assumption, not a gap.
read: AGENTS.md rules 9 and 13; Recovery Workbench Realignment overlay D-RCV-60
confirm: The document owner approves the realigned version after the run.
impact: The document is usable for planning; it is not a signed baseline.

text: The release dates 30 November 2026 and 31 December 2026 are copied unchanged from version 3 and marked (tentative); Phase 2 stays as the source gives it.
why: Template and Rules R1 U7 and AGENTS.md rule 10 keep dates unchanged and tentative, and a date is never raised as a gap.
read: Rules Engine Design v3 section 10; Template and Rules R1 U7; AGENTS.md rule 10
confirm: The programme plan confirms the dates after Wave 0.
impact: The delivery table is readable as the source's plan; the dates carry no commitment.

text: This version uses only the records allocated in ids.json: ADR-013 to ADR-023 and DL44 to DL49, with D-RCV-60 as the realignment decision; no new ADR, DL or D-RCV number is allocated here.
why: The run allocates decision identifiers centrally; a work package cites them and never invents one.
impact: Decision traceability stays consistent across the document set.

text: The owning service of a package is the service whose stage the decision belongs to, taken from the route-set to module mapping of the architecture and the Temporal and Drools design: S2 for restructure, settlement and deed in lieu, S3 guarantee, S4 litigation, S5 asset disposal, S6 debt sale, S7 write-off, S8 deviations, P3 case entry, exclusion, allocation, assignment and transfer.
why: The sources name the route sets and the stage owners separately and nowhere give a package-to-service table; the mapping follows the stage that owns each route set.
read: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 3, 4, 18 to 20 and 41; Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slides 13 and 17 to 25
confirm: RW-COE confirms the package owners when each Phase 2 package is authored.
impact: A Phase 2 package can move to another service only by re-opening this table and DP-04.
